input_references.role: Timestamped GPS trajectory points linked by trajectory_id

metadata.goal: Explore long-term mobility patterns and changes in individual travel behavior of the user.
metadata.category: Eight weeks of trajectories for one Montréal user, with work, shopping, and leisure purpose, day type, destination, route family, mode, point speed, and weekly spatial metrics.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 25 Single User Long Term Mobility Change
metadata.dataset_description: Eight weeks of trajectories for one Montréal user, with work, shopping, and leisure purpose, day type, destination, route family, mode, point speed, and weekly spatial metrics.
metadata.metric_note: Distances and directness are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; point speeds, trip durations, chain timing, and paired-leg timing are synchronized with the supplied point table. Route directness ratio is route distance divided by straight-line distance, so it is at least 1 and lower values indicate more direct routes.

plot.title: Work-trip Stability across Weeks
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How stable are work departure time, mode, destination, route family, and speed profile?
insight_list.insight: Across weeks, work trips retain similar departure times, modes, destination areas, recurring routes, and characteristic speed profiles.

plot.title: Shopping and Leisure Change across Weeks
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Do shopping and leisure trips shift later, farther, and toward more varied destinations and modes?
insight_list.insight: Shopping and leisure trips gradually shift toward later departures and farther destinations, with greater route diversity and more frequent mode changes.

plot.title: Distance, Mode, Speed, and Directness
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: For similar-purpose trips, how are farther destinations associated with mode, cruising speed, and route directness?
insight_list.insight: When similar-purpose trips extend to farther destinations, the user adopts faster modes, reaches higher cruising speeds, and follows more direct routes.

plot.title: Weekend and Weekday Spatial Extent
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do weekend and weekday destination footprints change over successive weeks?
insight_list.insight: Weekend travel becomes spatially broader over later weeks, while weekday trips remain concentrated around a small set of locations.

insights: Across weeks, work trips retain similar departure times, modes, destination areas, recurring routes, and characteristic speed profiles.
Shopping and leisure trips gradually shift toward later departures and farther destinations, with greater route diversity and more frequent mode changes.
When similar-purpose trips extend to farther destinations, the user adopts faster modes, reaches higher cruising speeds, and follows more direct routes.
Weekend travel becomes spatially broader over later weeks, while weekday trips remain concentrated around a small set of locations.
summary: The single user's work routine remains stable across eight weeks. Shopping and leisure gradually become later, farther, more spatially diverse, and more multimodal; farther trips use faster modes and more direct routes, expanding the weekend footprint while weekday travel stays concentrated.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
